description:
We’re ZERO-G 🚀 — a team passionate about technology, innovation, and solving real-world challenges. We’re interested in AI, software development, data science, and space exploration.

Our goal is to think beyond limits, collaborate, and turn creative ideas into impactful solutions.

We’re looking for motivated teammates with skills in programming, AI/ML, data analysis, UI/UX design, or creative problem-solving. Beginners with passion and a willingness to learn are welcome!
summary:
Astro Crew: 100 Days to Orbit is a real-time, 2D pixel-art cooperative and AI-assisted space operations crisis simulator built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. Players manage a four-person specialist crew—Commander, CapCom, Engineer, and Science Specialist—racing against a 180-second orbital impact clock to diagnose and stabilize 12 cascading subsystem emergencies across the spacecraft.

The project addresses the challenge by translating authentic NASA Mission Control and ISS emergency protocols into an accessible simulation. It enforces strict console role specialization, rapid 10-second triage under cognitive overload, and secondary physical hardware breakdowns that penalize hesitation with hull integrity breaches. Autonomous AI crewmates powered by 8-directional BFS pathfinding and human-like reaction telemetry enable seamless collaboration for both solo and local co-op play.

Astro Crew is important because it democratizes aerospace systems engineering and Crew Resource Management (CRM) through gamified education. By pairing high-stakes human-AI teaming with a post-flight telemetry dashboard that logs individual reaction speeds and automated root-cause failure analysis, it instills the critical values of communication, situational awareness, and data-driven debriefing.
details:
1. What Does It Do & How Does It Work?

Astro Crew: 100 Days to Orbit is a real-time, 2D pixel-art cooperative and AI-assisted spaceflight crisis simulator. Set aboard a deep-space exploration vessel undergoing orbital insertion, the simulation puts a four-person specialist crew in charge of neutralizing cascading system failures within a strict 180-second (3:00 minute) mission countdown and 100% Hull Integrity.

Core Gameplay & Mechanics:

  • The 4 Specialist Roles: Crew members operate certified stations across dedicated sector rooms:
    • Commander (Cockpit / North): Manages navigation helms, attitude thruster drift, and overall tactical coordination.
    • CapCom (CapCom Room / East): Manages telemetry servers, debris-tracking radar, and communications power buses.
    • Engineer (Engine Room / South): Manages manifold pressure valves, the central plasma furnace, and auxiliary drive turbines.
    • Science Specialist (Science Lab / West): Manages biological culture incubators, bio-specimen containment, and cryogenic DNA sequencers.
    1. Phase 1 — Tactical Decision (10-second window): Approaching within 60px of a station opens a technical diagnostic terminal with 3 operational options (1 nominal fix, 2 catastrophic errors).
    2. Phase 2 — Physical Breakdown Penalty (15-second window): An incorrect choice or timeout short-circuits the machine, spawning a physical Broken Node adjacent to the station, triggering a Red Alert siren and screen vignette. The specialist must physically reach the node and hold the repair key for 3.0 seconds. Failure deducts -20% Hull Integrity.
  • Autonomous AI Teammates (AIAgent): When playing solo or in partial teams, autonomous bots fill remaining slots using a 100×100 navigation grid, 8-directional BFS pathfinding, raycast line-of-sight smoothing, and human-like 80/20 stochastic decision accuracy.
  • Post-Flight Telemetry & Root-Cause Debriefing (AnalyticsReport): Upon mission completion (victory or failure), a NASA-style telemetry board evaluates each crew member's reaction latency (seconds), solved/missed station tally, and automated causal "blame" analysis.

2. What Benefits Does It Have?

  • Accessible Systems Engineering Education: Demystifies intricate aerospace engineering, environmental control, and flight dynamics concepts into intuitive, interactive problem-solving scenarios.
  • Scalable Cooperative Play (1 to 4 Players): Thanks to autonomous AI teammates, solo players enjoy the exact same high-stakes 4-station coordination dynamics as a full 4-player human party.
  • Zero-Install Web Accessibility: Runs completely client-side in any modern web browser at 60 FPS via WebGL without large downloads or specialized hardware.
  • Cognitive Skill Development: Strengthens rapid situational triage, communication under pressure, and spatial task management.

3. What Is the Intended Impact of the Project?

  • Inspiring the Next Generation of Space Explorers: Bridges the gap between complex NASA technical manuals and public engagement through the beloved, approachable medium of 16-bit retro arcade gaming.
  • Cultivating Crew Resource Management (CRM): Teaches users that aerospace mission success depends on psychological trust, role specialization, clear communication, and collective accountability rather than isolated individual actions.
  • Promoting Data-Driven Debriefing Culture: Models NASA's post-flight review process by showing that errors are quantifiable learning opportunities rather than mere game-over screens.

4. Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software Used

  • Programming Languages: JavaScript (ES2022+), HTML5, CSS3.
  • Rendering & Graphics Engine: PixiJS v8 (WebGL/Canvas pipeline, procedural texture generation, 2D sprite rendering, Y-depth sorting, and per-quadrant RenderTexture split-screen allocation).
  • UI & Component State: React 18 (reactive HUD modals, player state machines, telemetry debriefs).
  • Animations: Framer Motion v11 (smooth modal transitions, red alert vignette pulsing, starfield lobby animations).
  • Audio System: Howler.js v2.2 (WebAudio synthesis, spatial looping, muffled lo-fi ambient filters, dynamic Red Alert klaxon, and perceptual volume curves).
  • Styling & Retro Typography: Tailwind CSS v4 & Google Fonts ("Press Start 2P").
  • Build Tooling & Hosting: Vite v6 for local HMR compilation; Vercel for automated cloud CI/CD and production deployment; Git/GitHub for version control.
  • Hardware/Platform: Platform-independent (Windows, macOS, Linux, ChromeOS) across modern desktop browsers.

5. How Is Your Project Creative?

  • Dual-Mode Rendering Pipeline: Implements a unified WebGL scene graph loaded once into GPU memory that renders either a smooth lerping single-player camera at 2× zoom or dynamic 2-, 3-, or 4-player simultaneous split-screen quadrants on a single shared screen.
  • Simulated Human Imperfection in AI Agents: Rather than making AI bots unrealistically instantaneous or infallible, our AI engine mimics authentic human cognitive latency (3–6s thinking delay) and includes an 80/20 decision accuracy model, requiring bots to scramble and manually repair their own physical mistakes.
  • Two-Tiered Failure Cascade: Elevates standard quiz or trivia games into a physical spatial simulation: intellectual mistakes directly trigger physical engineering hardware breakdowns that players must walk over and physically repair with tools before hull breach occurs.
  • Automated Post-Mortem Blame Telemetry: Instead of a generic win/loss screen, our telemetry report dynamically parses chronological event logs to construct contextual root-cause failure narratives (e.g., "Pumped extra fuel into an already white-hot Plasma Furnace — then failed to repair Broken Plasma Core (-20% Hull)").

6. What Factors Did Your Team Consider?

  • Cognitive Load & Sensory Stress Calibration: Carefully calibrated the mission duration (180 seconds), decision window (10 seconds), and emergency repair countdown (15 seconds) alongside audio cues (engine hum, ambient hull creaks, Red Alert sirens) to induce authentic flight-deck urgency without causing frustrating cognitive paralysis.
  • Equal Engagement Across Roles: Designed the ship topology with balanced walking distances from the Central Hub and gave each specialist exactly 3 distinct high-impact crises to ensure no player or station felt secondary.
  • Accessibility & Input Ghosting Prevention: Designed an event-driven InputManager supporting simultaneous 4-player inputs on a single keyboard, separating edge-triggered menu selections (wasPressed) from continuous key-holds (interacting) to avoid hardware key-rollover conflicts.
  • Authenticity to Aerospace Flight Rules: Directly incorporated International Space Station (ISS) emergency triage procedures (fire/plasma containment, depressurization, toxic bio-hazards, and electrical power bus isolation) into the scenario narratives and nominal recovery actions.
